gaps: No seafood of any kind in the rotation.
No Japanese or Korean cuisine despite owning equipment well-suited to both.
Live-fire cooking (Big Green Egg, Ooni) is completely unused — no grilled or smoked mains.
Tex-Mex is a stated favourite but is represented by only one dish.
No Chinese wok cooking despite owning a carbon steel wok — only Thai and Asian-American noodle dishes.
Bacon is eaten and enjoyed but appears in no main dish despite being called out explicitly.

ideas.title: Shakshuka (Eggs in Spicy Tomato and Roasted Red Pepper Sauce)
ideas.why: Fills the complete absence of egg-based mains and proper Middle Eastern cooking in one fast, one-skillet weeknight dish the whole family can eat.

ideas.title: Miso Salmon
ideas.why: Fills both the seafood gap and the Japanese cuisine gap — a quick broil on a weeknight using pantry staples already common in this household.

ideas.title: Bibimbap (Mixed Rice with Vegetables)
ideas.why: Opens Korean cuisine entirely, puts the carbon steel wok and Dutch oven to use, and the seasoned-vegetables version is naturally vegetarian with beef as an easy side addition for meat eaters.

ideas.title: Beef Enchiladas
ideas.why: Tex-Mex is a stated family favourite with only one dish representing it — this homemade-sauce version is a crowd-pleasing, kid-friendly bake that fills that gap directly.

ideas.title: Bacon and Egg Fried Rice
ideas.why: Puts the carbon steel wok to proper use for Chinese cooking, uses bacon (a family staple) as the protein, and is the fast weeknight wok technique dish entirely missing from the collection.

ideas.title: Grill-Roasted Beef Short Ribs
ideas.why: The Big Green Egg has never been used for a main dish — this low-and-slow indirect charcoal project with a spice rub and glaze is exactly the weekend cook that equipment was built for.
